planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, strongly acidic soil in partial shade; August Beauty blooms over an unusually long season, from late spring through summer into early fall, rather than the shorter single flush of many gardenias.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, acidic soil in partial shade to morning sun with afternoon shade. August Beauty is one of the most widely planted gardenia cultivars in the Gulf South, prized for large, fully double, intensely fragrant white flowers produced over an extended season from late spring well into early fall rather than a single short spring flush. The dense, rounded, glossy-leaved shrub makes a good foundation or specimen planting near a porch, window, or path where its fragrance can be appreciated up close. Like all gardenias it is sensitive to soil pH, developing yellow, chlorotic leaves if the soil is not sufficiently acidic, so acidifying fertilizer and consistent moisture are key to keeping it healthy and free-flowering.

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, strongly acidic soil in partial shade; Frostproof is notably more cold-hardy than standard gardenia cultivars, extending reliable gardenia culture further north than the species typically tolerates.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, acidic soil in partial shade to morning sun. As its name suggests, Frostproof was selected specifically for improved cold hardiness compared to standard Gardenia jasminoides, tolerating colder winters with less dieback than most cultivars while still producing the classic, intensely fragrant, creamy white double flowers gardenias are grown for. Its compact, naturally dense habit also makes it a good choice for foundation plantings and smaller borders where a full-sized gardenia would grow too large. Consistent moisture and acidic soil are essential, since gardenias quickly develop yellow, chlorotic foliage in alkaline or poorly drained conditions.

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, strongly acidic soil in partial shade; Kleim's Hardy has notably smaller leaves and flowers than standard gardenia along with improved cold tolerance, and it blooms earlier in spring than most cultivars.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, acidic soil in partial shade to morning sun. Kleim's Hardy is distinguished from most gardenia cultivars by its small, narrow, fine-textured leaves and smaller single-form flowers, giving it a more refined, delicate look than the bold, glossy-leaved standard gardenia. It also blooms earlier in spring than most gardenia cultivars and shows improved cold hardiness, letting it succeed in gardens at the cooler edge of typical gardenia range. Fragrance remains strong despite the smaller flower size, and the compact habit suits foundation plantings, low hedges, and smaller garden spaces. Consistent moisture and acidic soil are essential to avoid the chlorotic yellowing common to gardenias in alkaline conditions.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade to full sun; Shishigashira is a naturally low, dense grower that blooms later in the sasanqua season than many cultivars, extending camellia color into winter.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade to full sun. Shishigashira is a compact, mounding sasanqua camellia noted for its unusually low, dense, wider-than-tall habit compared to the more upright growth of most sasanquas, making it useful as a large-scale groundcover, low hedge, or foundation planting. It produces semi-double, rose-pink flowers with ruffled petals in late fall into winter, later in the season than earlier-blooming sasanqua cultivars, extending camellia interest further into the cold months. Like other camellias it needs consistently moist, acidic soil and benefits from a layer of mulch to protect shallow roots and conserve moisture through the year.

common_name: Penny Mac Hydrangea (Reliable Reblooming Blue Mophead Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Penny Mac blooms on both old and new wood, so it reliably reflowers through summer even after a late frost damages the previous year's buds.

directions: Plant in consistently moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade, protected from hot afternoon sun. Penny Mac was an early and long-proven rebloomer among mophead hydrangeas, flowering on both old wood from the previous season and new wood produced the same year, which means a late spring frost that kills the old flower buds does not prevent a good summer bloom as it would on older mophead cultivars. Flower color shifts with soil pH the way most macrophylla hydrangeas do, ranging from blue in acidic soil to pink in more alkaline soil, and can be adjusted with soil amendments if a particular color is desired. Keep soil consistently moist, since hydrangea's large leaves wilt quickly in dry heat, and prune only lightly to remove dead wood, since heavy pruning removes the old-wood flower buds that provide the earliest bloom flush.
